title: Separated affine and local charts surject onto the function field
statement: Let X be an integral [def-pc-integral-scheme] separated [def-weil-proper-morphism] scheme [def-pc-scheme], let U=Spec(A) be a nonempty affine open subscheme of X, let x be a point of X\U, let B=O_{X,x} be its local ring, and assume B is Noetherian [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring] of Krull dimension 1 [def-weil-pbc-krull-dimension-ring]. Let K=k(X) be the function field [def-sc-function-field]. Via the inclusions A\to K and B\to K [lem-sc-integral-scheme-stalks-in-function-field], the canonical ring map A \otimes_{\mathbb Z} B \to K is surjective.

source.place: Varieties Lemma 09NB (varieties-lemma-find-globally-generated), proof, second and third sentences

proof.text: Let $\eta$ be the generic point of the integral scheme $X$. Since $U$ is nonempty, $\eta\in U$. The stalk lemma [lem-sc-integral-scheme-stalks-in-function-field] makes $B=\mathcal O_{X,x}$ a domain embedded in $K$ with fraction field $K$. Let $c:\operatorname{Spec}(B)\to X$ be the canonical morphism of [lem-weil-pbc-spec-local-ring-canonical-morphism]; its image is the set of generalizations of $x$, so $c^{-1}(U)=\operatorname{Spec}(B)\setminus\{\mathfrak m_B\}$. Since $B$ has dimension one, choose $0\ne f\in\mathfrak m_B$. Then $D(f)=\{(0)\}=c^{-1}(U)$, and [lem-weil-pbc-principal-localization-open-immersion] identifies this open subscheme with $\operatorname{Spec}(B_f)$. The prime correspondence in [lem-weil-pbc-primes-of-localization] shows that $B_f$ has only the prime $(0)$; the new statement [lem-sc-local-domain-dim-one-principal-localization-fraction-field] therefore identifies $B_f\cong K$. Thus $U\times_X\operatorname{Spec}(B)=\operatorname{Spec}(K)$, using [lem-weil-pbc-open-immersion-base-change] for the pullback of the open immersion $U\hookrightarrow X$. Finally [lem-weil-pbc-fibre-product-affine-spectra], with base ring $R=\mathbb Z$, identifies $U\times_{\operatorname{Spec}(\mathbb Z)}\operatorname{Spec}(B)$ with $\operatorname{Spec}(A\otimes_{\mathbb Z}B)$, and the induced map to $\operatorname{Spec}(K)$ is from the inclusions into $K$.

source.place: Varieties Lemma 09NB, proof, opening paragraph: identification of U \times_X Spec(B_i) with Spec(K)

proof.text: Because $X$ is separated, its diagonal $\Delta_X:X\to X\times_{\operatorname{Spec}(\mathbb Z)}X$ is a closed immersion by [def-weil-proper-morphism]. Base changing this closed immersion along the morphism $U\times_{\operatorname{Spec}(\mathbb Z)}\operatorname{Spec}(B)\to X\times_{\operatorname{Spec}(\mathbb Z)}X$ gives a closed immersion $U\times_X\operatorname{Spec}(B)\hookrightarrow U\times_{\operatorname{Spec}(\mathbb Z)}\operatorname{Spec}(B)$ by [lem-weil-pbc-closed-immersion-base-change]. Under Step 1 and [lem-weil-pbc-fibre-product-affine-spectra] (again with $R=\mathbb Z$), this is the closed immersion $\operatorname{Spec}(K)\hookrightarrow\operatorname{Spec}(A\otimes_{\mathbb Z}B)$.

source.place: Varieties Lemma 09NB, proof, sentence beginning 'Since X is separated'

proof.text: Apply the affine closed-immersion criterion [lem-weil-pbc-closed-immersion-affine-cover-criterion](1) to the affine target $\operatorname{Spec}(A\otimes_{\mathbb Z}B)$ identified by [lem-weil-pbc-fibre-product-affine-spectra]. It says that the induced map on global sections is surjective. The global-sections map of this closed immersion is exactly the canonical map $A\otimes_{\mathbb Z}B\to K$ induced by the inclusions $A\to K$ and $B\to K$. Hence $A\otimes_{\mathbb Z}B\to K$ is surjective.

lean.statement: theorem Scheme.separated_affine_functionField_surjective (X : Scheme.{u}) [IsIntegral X] [hsep : X.IsSeparated] (U : X.Opens) (hU : IsAffineOpen U) [hUn : Nonempty U] (x : X) (hx : x ∉ U) [IsNoetherianRing (X.presheaf.stalk x)] (hdim : ringKrullDim (X.presheaf.stalk x) = 1) : let A : Type u := Γ(X, U) let B : Type u := X.presheaf.stalk x let K : Type u := X.functionField let φ : TensorProduct ℤ A B →ₐ[ℤ] K := Algebra.TensorProduct.lift (X.germToFunctionField U).hom.toIntAlgHom (algebraMap B K).toIntAlgHom (fun _ _ => Commute.all _ _) Function.Surjective φ
